steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) and RNA (ribonucleic acid) are both nucleic acids but differ in four key ways:

1. Sugar
   • DNA: Deoxyribose (lacks an oxygen on the 2′ carbon).  
   • RNA: Ribose (has an –OH on the 2′ carbon).

2. Bases
   • DNA: Adenine (A), Thymine (T), Cytosine (C), Guanine (G).  
   • RNA: A, Uracil (U) replaces T, plus C and G.

3. Structure
   • DNA: Usually double-stranded, forming a stable double helix.  
   • RNA: Usually single-stranded; can fold into diverse 3-D shapes (tRNA, rRNA, etc.).

4. Function & Stability
   • DNA: Long-term genetic storage; highly stable, resides mainly in the nucleus (eukaryotes).  
   • RNA: Short-term messages (mRNA), catalysts (ribozymes), adapters (tRNA), structural (rRNA); less stable, found in nucleus and cytoplasm.

In short: DNA is the durable, double-stranded storage medium with thymine and deoxyribose; RNA is the more versatile, single-stranded working copy with uracil and ribose.
